title: Binod Singh, Kahan Singh, and the Gulab Rai Opening

blocks.text: This page closes the story of estranged veterans by recounting how These two veterans invaded Banda Singh along with the Mughals and then benefited from imperial favor after Banda Singh's defeat. The episode presents them as men who exchanged old Sikh prestige for rank, troops, and access under Mughal power.

It then narrows to the circle of Kahan Singh, Baba Binod Singh, and Miri Singh, showing how these named figures stand at the edge of a new sequence after the political settlement. The narrative tone is one of uneasy transition rather than triumph.

At the bottom, the page turns toward Gulab Rai and the problem of false guruship. That hinge matters because a military-political aftermath gives way to a religious and social satire about imitation authority.
